text:
mel: Heads-up — planning to unpin runtime v2.15 from hosted canary tonight at 02:00 UTC.
kevin: what's the primary risk? SDK compatibility?
sara: There was a header change in runtime 2.15.1 that can break SDK 3.1 clients if they use streaming fallback.
kevin: Right, the issue is the handshake when kv-cache is enabled. We saw 0.3% error bump in canary telemetry earlier.
mel: Can we patch SDK first? timeline?
kevin: We can ship a minor SDK 3.1.1 with a small handshake tolerance. Should be ready in ~2h.
mel: ok. @devin you'll be nightshift oncall — if we delay unpin, can you monitor request error rate and latency?
devin: Yep I'll watch. I'll set an alert: `canary.runtime.errors > 0.5% for 5m` and slack notify #eng-platform
deploy-bot: [INFO] scheduled unpin: runtime v2.15 -> UNPIN request queued for 02:00 UTC
ops-watchdog: auto: added telemetry check `kv_handshake_errors` to the canary dashboard
kevin: If SDK patch isn't ready by 01:30 UTC we should delay and run a scoped rollback plan. Rollback command is:
```
deployctl pin runtime --model-group canary --version 2.14.7 --reason "safety hold"
```
mel: Agree. Also update release notes with `KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: streaming-handshake` so solutions-engineering can advise customers.
sara: I'll add a short blurb and a redirect in the docs to the SDK patch guide.
devin: During the window I'll route traffic fallback to dedicated pool B if error > 1%: `routectl set-fallback --pool dedicated-b`
mel: Perfect. post-unpin checks:
- sanity: 200 OK on /health
- kv-handshake error < 0.2%
- p50 latency stable
kevin: I'll keep a shortcanary for 30m after unpin before global rollout.
mel: ok let's reconvene at 01:40 UTC for final go/no-go. :eyes:
sara: noted. I'll push docs and the small changelog now.
deploy-bot: [EVENT] unpin queued -> will execute at 02:00 UTC unless canceled
mel: thanks everyone. file this under release notes + incident-runbook if we hit rollback. :thumbsup:
